spec_match.rationale: The explainer is technically accurate and matches the spec change: CSS vs physical pixels, DPR scaling (score × DPR² before 145), the unchanged CLS formula with CSS-px inputs, and the affected LayoutShiftAttribution fields.

interactive.rationale: The only interactivity is the generic bolted-on 'scenario focus' walkthrough that scrolls/highlights existing sections — it never reads devicePixelRatio, never observes a layout shift, and exercises no feature surface.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises an explanation of CSS vs physical pixels, DPR, and why the change makes CLS meaningful on high-DPI devices; the page delivers exactly that framing.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers DPR 1/2/3 scenarios and conversion guidance, but zoom interplay and hadRecentInput live only on sibling pages and are not linked from the body.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5155103518228480, web.dev CLS, and the cls-demo sibling.

conformance.rationale: Shares the feature suite (6/6 structural existence checks here) — adequate for structure, silent on unit semantics.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Desktop and 360px mobile screenshots captured, DOM state and console verified clean in headless Chromium 141; walkthrough buttons exist but page has no feature-exercising control to drive.

telemetry_health.rationale: Server-injected /public/demo-telemetry.js verified in the served DOM.

design_system.rationale: Tables, formula block, and walkthrough all use the shared variables; no raw hex.

accessibility.rationale: Semantic tables with headers, aria-labelledby on the walkthrough section, and an aria-live=polite output for the walkthrough summary.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-measured at 360px: the .compare-table forces content to 418px and body overflow-x:hidden clips the last column (~58px cut) — table data is lost on narrow phones.

openQuestions.title: Add a real live probe: DPR/physical-px converter or mini shift reader
openQuestions.detail: The page is a static explainer whose only control is the generic scenario-focus walkthrough. A small live panel reading window.devicePixelRatio, converting a chosen CSS-px rect to physical pixels, and (where supported) reading one real LayoutShift entry would make the unit change tangible and satisfy the no-static-card rule.

openQuestions.title: Make the comparison tables scrollable on mobile
openQuestions.detail: At 360px the .compare-table reaches 418px and is clipped by body overflow-x:hidden, cutting the 'Chrome 145+' column. Wrap tables in an overflow-x:auto container so they scroll instead of being cut.

summary: Accurate, well-structured explainer of the CSS-pixel change with a good pre/post-145 comparison table and correct formula notes; its weaknesses are the absence of any real feature-exercising interactivity (only the generic walkthrough) and a clipped comparison table at 360px. Browser-verified with headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI (screenshot + DOM dump) and raw CDP (real click dispatch, console/network capture, 360x740 DPR3 mobile emulation) — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session. Chromium 141 predates Chrome 145, so v145-only API paths were validated on their fallback branches, not the new-API success path. The single failed fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet request is environmental (blocked host) and was not counted against any page.
